title: A Study of Renyi Entropy in pp Collisions by ALICE Data- A Comparison with UrQMD Simulation and AI-Assisted Modeling
summary: In the present investigation a systematic study of order dependence and energy dependence of Renyi entropy calculated from the ALICE experimental data of charged-particle multiplicity distributions in pp collisions at the centre-of-mass energies \root s= 2.76, 7 and 13 TeV within the pseudo-rapidity interval and transverse momentum range as selected by ALICE collaborationc has been carried out. ALICE collaboration compared the experimental multiplicity distribution of charged particles in pp collisions by PYTHIA 8.306 and EPOS-LHC model and hence Renyi entropy has also been evaluated from the corresponding PYTHIA 8.306 and EPOS-LHC model results reported by the ALICE Collaboration. An independent comparison has been carried out using UrQMD simulation generated for the same collision energies and kinematic acceptance by the author himself. In addition, an AI-assisted multiplicity distribution is considered as an auxiliary statistical reference for Renyi entropy estimation. In all the cases, the Renyi entropy exhibits a decreasing trend with increasing order q, indicating the presence of multifractality in pp collisions. The values of Renyi entropy for a particular order increases systematically with the increase of collision energy from \root s = 2.76TeV to 13 TeV, reflecting the increasing disorder and dynamical fluctuations of the particle-production process.

title: Measurements of inclusive $J/ψ$ production in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 14.6, 17.3, 19.6, and 27 GeV with the STAR experiment
summary: Inclusive $J/ψ$ production at mid-rapidity ($|y| < 1.0$) in Au+Au collisions at center-of-mass energies per nucleon-nucleon pair ($\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$) of 14.6, 17.3, 19.6, and 27 GeV is measured with the STAR detector at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider. The nuclear modification factor $R_{\rm AA}$ is used to quantify modifications of $J/ψ$ production relative to an interpolated $p$+$p$ reference. The measured $R_{\rm AA}$ shows a hint of a decreasing trend from peripheral to central collisions, reaching a value of approximately 0.5 in the 0-20% centrality class across all collision energies. Unlike similar measurements in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 200 GeV, where $J/ψ$ $R_{\rm AA}$ shows little dependence on transverse momentum ($p_{\rm {T}}$), the corresponding $R_{\rm AA}$ at the lower collision energies of 14.6-27 GeV shows a tendency to increase with $p_{\rm {T}}$. Additionally, the inclusive $J/ψ$ $R_{\rm AA}$, integrated over $J/ψ$ $p_{\rm {T}}$, in central collisions exhibits no significant variation within uncertainties over the energy range of 14.6 to 200 GeV. These results can be qualitatively described by transport models that incorporate hot and cold nuclear matter effects.

title: Interpretation follows computation for deformed atomic nuclei
summary: The interpretation of nuclear levels in experiments and ab initio computations is challenging because it requires the production and analysis of many expectation values and transition strengths. Here we introduce an approach that yields directly interpretable states. Our ab initio coupled-cluster computations start from a reference state with axial symmetry and positive parity. Equation-of-motion techniques then yield intrinsic states with definite parity and angular-momentum projection onto the symmetry axis. Finally, the projection onto good angular momenta yields rotational bands based on these intrinsic states. In the neutron-rich nucleus $^{34}$Mg, where only the ground-state band is known, we find several low-lying positive- and negative-parity bands. The lowest, a $K^π=3^-$ band, is dominated by a single neutron particle-hole excitation rather than by octupole collectivity. These results challenge the common wisdom about how deformation and pairing work in nuclei.

title: Structure and Binding of the \texorpdfstring{$pnΩ^-$}{pnOmega} System with a Near-Unitary \texorpdfstring{$NΩ$}{NOmega} Interaction from Physical-Point Lattice QCD
summary: The binding and spatial structure of the \(pnΩ^-\) system are investigated in the \(I(J^P)=0(5/2^+)\) channel using the physical-point HAL QCD \(NΩ({}^{5}S_2)\) interaction. The pairwise Hamiltonian includes the spin-triplet \(pn\) interaction and the finite-size Coulomb attraction in the \(pΩ^-\) pair. The three-body Schrödinger equation is solved with the Gaussian Expansion Method (GEM), including all three Jacobi rearrangement configurations. For the central HAL QCD potential at \(t/a=14\), the calculated three-body binding energy is \(18.63\) MeV, corresponding to a separation energy of \(16.39\) MeV relative to the \(d+Ω^-\) threshold. The spatial structure is examined through interparticle root-mean-square distances, pair and spectator radial distributions, and the correlation between the two Jacobi coordinates. Relative to a frozen-deuteron folded reference, the full three-body solution exhibits a substantially more compact spectator distribution and a contracted \(pn\) pair. The dependence on the Euclidean-time choice of the HAL QCD potential is also assessed. The results characterize the three-body rearrangement induced by the attractive \(NΩ\) interaction within the adopted pairwise model.

title: Impact of Effective Nucleon Mass and Symmetry Energy on Nuclear Pasta Phases and the Unified Equation of State of Neutron Stars
summary: We investigate how the effective nucleon mass and symmetry energy affect pasta phase properties and the unified equation of state (EOS) of neutron stars. The nonuniform pasta structure is described within the self-consistent Thomas-Fermi approximation, while nucleonic interactions are treated in the relativistic mean-field framework with several typical parameter sets adopted. Our results indicate that the symmetry energy and its slope are crucial in determining the onset of pasta phases and their geometric configurations. In the high-density region where matter becomes uniform, the effective nucleon mass plays a dominant role. A larger effective nucleon mass tends to soften the EOS, which yields a smaller radius for a canonical $1.4 M_{\odot}$ neutron star and reduces the corresponding tidal deformability.

title: Anisotropic Coulomb Interaction in Strongly Magnetized Electron Gas at Zero Temperature in Relativistic Quantum Framework
summary: We present a microscopic derivation of Debye screening in a Landau-quantized electron gas subject to a strong magnetic field. By calculating the photon self-energy within the RPA framework, we explore how Landau levels influence the screening properties of the electron gas. Due to the quantum periodicity of Landau levels, the screening behavior is relatively insensitive to variations in the carrier density within each occupation cycle compared to the drastic changes induced by the magnetic field strength. Within a single occupation cycle, the Kohn anomaly dominates the low-density regime; at higher densities, its characteristic momentum shifts into the asymptotic high-momentum regime, rendering its singular contribution less prominent over the active screening domain and allowinga smooth orientation-dependent anisotropy to govern the system. Furthermore, a subtle competition in directional screening is observed between the parallel and perpendicular directions to the field depending on the density domain. At lower field strengths, multiple quantum oscillations emerge from the simultaneous participation of various Landau levels, marking a qualitative transition toward the isotropic three-dimensional limit. Our findings reveal anisotropic screening effects and provide insights into the behavior of charged impurities in such systems.

title: Particle-vibration coupling model with explicit doorway states based on the Skyrme density functional
summary: Modern $γ$-ray detectors can achieve energy resolutions of a few keV, motivating microscopic studies of strength fragmentation in nuclear excitation spectra. Particle-vibration coupling (PVC) describes the spreading of giant resonances, but conventional formulations based on an energy-dependent effective Hamiltonian in the 1 particle-1 hole (1p1h) space do not explicitly provide individual excited states and their wave functions. We develop a PVC model with explicit doorway states by directly diagonalising the PVC matrix in the space of 1p1h and 1p1h coupled to a phonon (1p1h$\otimesν$) configurations. Using the Skyrme energy density functional SkM*, we study the isovector giant dipole resonance (GDR) in $^{208}$Pb. The one-body transition densities show that the neutron and proton components of the dominant GDR states remain out of phase after including PVC, preserving their isovector character. Wave-function analysis reveals that the $2^+$ and $3^-$ phonons play a key role in GDR fragmentation. The fragmented states are dominated by 1p1h$\otimesν$ configurations, accounting for more than 80\% of the wave-function norm. Nevertheless, coherent contributions of 1p1h configurations preserve the collective character of the $E1$ transitions. Thus, PVC strongly modifies the microscopic structure and fragmentation of the GDR without changing its essential isovector collective character.

title: Light-particle emission in nucleon-induced fission of $^{235,238}$U at energies from 10 MeV to 1 GeV
summary:
Background: In nucleon-induced fission up to GeV energies, early nonequilibrium emission alters the residual nuclei before statistical evaporation and scission. The emitted light particles therefore probe each reaction stage while supplying needed nuclear data.
  Purpose: We study neutron and light charged-particle emission in $^{235,238}$U$(n,f)$ and $^{235,238}$U$(p,f)$ reactions at incident energies from 10 MeV to 1 GeV.
  Methods: The reactions are simulated event by event by coupling the isospin-dependent quantum molecular dynamics model with the GEMINI++ statistical decay code.
  Results: The calculations follow the measured rise in average neutron multiplicity with incident energy, while yielding higher values above 100 MeV and in the proton-induced prescission component. Within the coupled calculations, the neutron multiplicity growth comes mainly from statistical evaporation before scission, whereas emission from the fission fragments changes weakly. Although the average preequilibrium neutron yield remains small, early emission spreads the residual nuclei across multiple elements and wide excitation energies. At high energies, protons are emitted predominantly before equilibration, directly reducing the charge retained by the residual nuclei.
  Conclusions: In the coupled calculations, statistical evaporation before scission governs the neutron multiplicity growth, whereas early nonequilibrium emission shapes the residual nuclei and dominates high-energy proton emission. These results provide a reference for modeling intermediate-energy fission, in which prescission emission changes the charge, mass, and excitation energy of the fissioning system.

title: Nucleon Short-Range Correlations and Supersoft Nuclear Symmetry Energy: Compatibility with Massive Neutron Stars and GW170817
summary: Massive neutron stars (NSs) require a sufficiently stiff core equation of state (EOS), while the relatively small tidal deformability inferred from GW170817 favors softer nuclear matter at intermediate densities. Given the importance of the nuclear symmetry energy in neutron-rich matter, an intriguing question arises: Can the symmetry energy become supersoft at high densities while remaining compatible with these seemingly competing constraints? Within the nonlinear Walecka framework, we demonstrate that nucleon short-range correlations (SRCs), manifested as a high-momentum tail (HMT) in the nucleon momentum distribution, can accommodate such behavior without introducing additional interaction parameters. We derive for the first time analytical expressions for the symmetry energy curvature $K_{\rm{sym}}$ for both free Fermi gas (FFG) and HMT momentum distributions. Using model parameter sets that reproduce empirical nuclear matter properties around saturation density, we find that SRC-HMT yields substantially more negative $K_{\rm{sym}}$ than the FFG case, allowing the symmetry energy to reach a maximum at low supra-saturation densities and subsequently decrease while the total pressure remains sufficient to support massive NSs. The resulting EOSs also predict smaller NS radii and tidal deformabilities consistent with GW170817. These results connect the microscopic nucleon momentum distribution with the density dependence of the symmetry energy and macroscopic NS properties.

title: Rigid triaxial roto-vibrator in a finite system
comment: 7 pages, 8 figures, 2 Tables, accepted for publication in Physics Letters B
summary: We investigate the emergence of rigid triaxiality in a finite system, within the framework of the interacting boson model of nuclei. Appropriate Hamiltonians for a maximally-triaxial rigid shape are constructed. Closed expressions for wave functions, energies and E2 rates for states of the ground band are derived. Classical and quantum analyses reveal that for a fixed Hamiltonian, the system evolves from a $γ$-soft SO(6) structure for small $N$, to a $γ$-rigid structure for large $N$. Attention is paid to symmetry and spectral properties of both rotational and vibrational states.

title: The antibaryon-baryon interaction based on chiral EFT with a focus on $\bar pp$ and $\barΛΛ$ reactions
summary: The antibaryon-baryon ($\bar BB$) interaction is reviewed in the context of the hyperon(Y)-production reactions $\bar NN\to\bar YY$ with special emphasis on the $\bar ΛΛ$ system. The experimental situation for $\bar BB\to\bar YY$ from threshold up to antiproton lab momenta of $2$ GeV/c is discussed and likewise past theoretical approaches and results. The formalism for a description of the $\bar BB$ interaction in terms of potentials derived within SU(3) chiral effective field theory (EFT) is outlined. Constraints from SU(3) flavor symmetry on the $\bar BB$ interaction in the various reaction channels are discussed. As concrete application a new analysis of the reaction $\bar pp\to\bar ΛΛ$ is performed utilizing potentials for the $\bar NN$ and $\bar ΛΛ$ channels, and for the $\bar NN\to\barΛΛ$ transition, up to next-to-leading order in the chiral expansion, supplemented by a phenomenological part to account for annihilation processes. An excellent reproduction of data from the PS185 experiment at CERN up to momenta of $1.55$ GeV/c is achieved. When including higher-order contact terms in the analysis the range of agreement can be extended up to momenta around $1.65$ GeV/c, where a complete set of scattering observables is available. Predictions for $\barΛΛ$ scattering are provided and compared to results from the literature.

title: Probing the structure of the two proton Borromean nucleus $^{17}\rm{Ne}$ through inclusive breakup data
summary: The proton-rich nucleus $^{17}$Ne exhibits a Borromean structure, $^{15}$O+p+p, since both $^{16}$F and diproton systems are unbound. The low-energy spectrum of this nucleus consists of a series of resonances that remain poorly identified. In this work, a three-body model is used to describe the structure of $^{17}$Ne, with special attention to the emergence of resonant states. The four-body continuum-discretized coupled-channel (CDCC) formalism is used to study the reaction of $^{17}$Ne on a $^{208}$Pb target near the Coulomb barrier. Comparing the calculated elastic and breakup cross sections with the recently available experimental data~\cite{OVEJAS2023138007} provides an excellent framework for probing the resonant structure of this nucleus.

title: u3lib: An AI-Ready Computational Framework for U(3) Symmetry Algebra, Wigner Coupling, and Racah Recoupling Coefficients
comment: 15 pages, 1 figure, 3 tables. Code available at https://github.com/Deep-SANE/u3lib
summary: u3lib is a C++ library for U(3)/SU(3) representation-theory calculations in nuclear structure and related applications. It evaluates Wigner coupling and Racah recoupling coefficients using the procedure proposed in 2024 by Dang et al., which avoids the binomial coefficients and alternating sums used in earlier formulations. The library also provides irreducible representations (irreps), dimensions, Casimir invariants, conjugation, and tensor-product decompositions with outer multiplicities. It supports the canonical Gelfand-Tsetlin basis and the physical SU(3) $\supset$ SO(3) basis, including inner multiplicities and the transformation between the two bases. Generator routines return matrix elements in the canonical basis and reduced matrix elements in the physical basis. Python bindings mirror the C++ API. Domain skills supplied with the repository allow an AI assistant with code-execution access to call these routines from natural-language requests.
